title: Microsoft Purview: collection policies support in Insider Risk Management
summary: Hold: the briefing omits Microsoft's published requirement for Endpoint DLP licensing when a collection policy includes devices. It also labels the default as unstated even though the roadmap explicitly plans automatic collection-policy creation for device-indicator IRM policies; the settings and treatment of existing policies remain unclear.

claims.quote: They let you filter which events from both untrusted and trusted sources are ingested into Purview.

claims.quote: Once ingested, that data can be classified and used by various Microsoft Purview signal consuming solutions, such as Microsoft Purview Activity explorer, Microsoft Purview Insider Risk Management

claims.claim: A deployed device collection policy takes precedence when it conflicts with an IRM policy's monitoring of device indicators.
claims.quote: When a device collection policy is configured and deployed, if there's a conflict between what the Insider Risk Management policy is configured to monitor and what the collection policy is configured to filter for, the collection policy configuration takes precedence.

claims.quote: If you don't add conditions, what gets detected depends on the data sources you select later: Devices: All data is detected, even if it doesn't match your organization's classifiers.

claims.claim: The licence for this collection-policy use is simply that of Insider Risk Management.
claims.quote: creating a collection policy that includes devices requires endpoint DLP licensing, as the device data source is available under that licensing tier.
claims.fix: Replace 'The licence is that of Insider Risk Management.' with 'Collection policies have no separate licensing requirement, but require licensing for their workload; a collection policy that includes devices requires Endpoint DLP licensing.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/office365/servicedescriptions/microsoft-365-service-descriptions/microsoft-365-tenantlevel-services-licensing-guidance/microsoft-purview-service-description#microsoft-purview-collection-policies.

claims.claim: The licensing model for this device-indicator collection-policy change is mixed.
claims.quote: There are no licensing requirements to apply collection policies. Instead, you must be licensed for the workload for which you're creating the policy.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to 'included'. State in licensing.notes that collection policies require the licence for their workload, and device collection policies require Endpoint DLP licensing; retain the separate requirement for an appropriate IRM subscription. Cite the service description's Microsoft Purview Collection Policies section. Do not apply the generic pay-as-you-go cases for other data sources to this device change.
